conventions.convention: Countable Choice is assumed explicitly; no full Axiom of Choice is asserted.
Use Cartesian inertial coordinates in Newtonian spacetime, SI units, tension-positive stress, traction σn, and kinematic viscosity ν=μ/ρ₀.
The steady Stokes comparison adopts zero-inertia force balance as an alternative to imposing material-acceleration momentum balance on that comparison field.

The bounded-domain residual estimate assumes a stated zero-trace Poincaré constant. The periodic channel separately admits constant h; its representative cell is not treated as a bounded C¹ Euclidean domain.
Horizontal periodic fields and pressures are interpreted through periodic lifts, with unnormalized Lebesgue integration over one fundamental cell; no-slip wall data give zero perturbation trace.
The Couette threshold |S|h²/ν<2 is sufficient and nonsharp, and its conclusion holds only on the assumed smooth solution interval.
The fields and parameters are selected model inputs, with no measured inputs or empirical conclusions.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming Countable Choice and the stated physical conventions, let Ω be a bounded connected C¹ domain, μ,ρ₀>0 constant, and CΩ>0 satisfy the stated zero-trace Poincaré inequality. Already-existing C² divergence-free stationary Navier–Stokes and restricted Stokes velocities, with C¹ pressures, zero body acceleration and the same no-slip boundary velocity, give w=uNS−uS and f=−ρ₀(uNS·∇)uNS satisfying ‖∇w‖₂≤CΩ‖f‖₂/μ and ‖w‖₂≤CΩ²‖f‖₂/μ. The separately specified periodic-channel branch gives the corresponding bounds with CΩ=h. These are conditional residual estimates, without existence, exterior-domain or empirical conclusions.

Assuming Countable Choice, positive Lx,Lz,h,T,ρ₀,μ, ν=μ/ρ₀ and constant real S, let u∈C¹([0,T];C²(Q̄;R³)) and p∈C([0,T];C¹(Q̄)) be horizontally periodic, already-existing incompressible strong Navier–Stokes fields with zero body acceleration and wall values 0 and Sh(1,0,0). For w=u−(Sy,0,0) and E(t)=∫Q|w|², if |S|h²/ν<2, then E(t)≤exp[−(2ν/h²−|S|)t]E(0) for every t∈[0,T]. The condition is sufficient, not asserted sharp, and supplies neither global existence nor a physical transition threshold.

concerns.concern: The Statement jointly introduces the velocities and scalar pressures and then says they “are divergence-free velocity fields.” Grammatically this assigns the velocity type and divergence constraint to the pressures too. Separate the velocity hypotheses from the scalar-pressure regularity; the intended types and subsequent proof are otherwise clear.
